_comment: The 'Mangal' — a tank wearing a welded shed. Authored from reference photographs at
incoming/factions/russian-federation/units/mangal/ (gitignored: third-party rights, and
they inform PARAMETERS only — silhouette, proportion, palette — never pixels).
SECOND PASS, after seeing it in game and against a better reference frame. Three things
the first pass got wrong, all of them shape rather than detail:
1. IT IS WIDE. The shed is nearly as wide as it is tall and only about 1.5x longer than
wide — a squat box, not the long narrow wedge the side-on still suggested.
2. THE ROOF IS FLAT, or very nearly. The sides are VERTICAL and the top is a shallow
pitch of corrugated sheet. The first pass read the side profile as a triangular prism
and set ridgeWidth 0.18, which is a tent; the truth is a box with a lid on it, so the
ridge is now a separate shallow part at ridgeWidth 0.78.
3. THERE IS A TURRET. It traverses only a little, but it exists and it is visible
through the open front. The first pass asserted the carapace was welded solid and
that there was deliberately no TURRET sub-object — that was wrong, and it was wrong
in the direction of making a limitation sound like a design decision.
+X is FORWARD, matching how retail vehicles are laid out. Z is up, z = 0 is the ground,
so a part's `at` is the CENTRE of its box.
STILL DELIBERATELY NOT GEOMETRY: the cope-cage grid, the camo netting, and the road
wheels. All three are wire, mesh or repetition — texture work at a 245-triangle peer
budget. The wheels cost 55% of the first pass's triangles and were invisible inside the
track boxes; retail reaches the same conclusion, carrying flat tread strips with the links
painted on.
name: MANGAL

mangal.tga._: Weathered olive drab for the hull and the shed's flanks. `ao` and `lip` are the
mangal.tga.__: two that matter: a retail 256x256 vehicle sheet is not more colourful than ours
mangal.tga.___: and not higher frequency — it has dark occlusion in every recess and a bright lip
mangal.tga.____: on every top edge, and that is what makes a flat polygon read as a panelled one.

mangal_roof.tga._: Corrugated rust sheet. Narrow panels at strong occlusion IS corrugation once it is
mangal_roof.tga.__: texture rather than geometry — the ribs are the shadow between the sheets.

parts._: Track runs, pushed out to the new width. Links and road wheels are painted, not
parts.name: TRACKS

parts._: The hull under the shed. Visible through the open front and whenever the camera
parts.__: drops, so it cannot be omitted however well the carapace hides it from above.
parts.name: HULL

parts._: THE CARAPACE — a box with VERTICAL sides, not a prism. The front is cut clean
parts.__: through so the turret inside is visible, which is the single most recognisable
parts.___: thing about this vehicle and the one feature a texture genuinely cannot fake:
parts.____: the silhouette has to have a hole in it. Cut coordinates are LOCAL to the part.
parts.name: CARAPACE

parts._: The lid: a SHALLOW pitched roof of corrugated sheet, overhanging the box on every
parts.__: side. ridgeWidth 0.78 leaves a broad flat top — the reference's roof is barely
parts.___: peaked, and 0.18 (the first pass) made a tent.
parts.name: ROOF

parts._: TURRET. Its own named sub-object, because that is how the engine finds something
parts.__: to rotate — a merged mesh cannot traverse however good it looks. Sitting in the
parts.___: carapace's cut-out where the reference shows it.
parts.name: TURRET

parts._: Gun, out of the turret and through the opening.
parts.name: BARREL
